# Brief for the coach: adding incline curls to Monday

## Where the program stands today

Joe has been on this engine since 1 Nov 2026. The version in force is the third one, an amendment adopted on 4 Nov 2026, with a hypertrophy emphasis and the home gym as its base. The training block it belongs to opened on 1 Nov 2026 and is in its first rotation week (week A). The week is:

- **Monday – OHP, back and arms (75-minute cap), plus a separate kettlebell swing session the same day.** Overhead press: warm-ups of 5 and 3, a top set of 5 at RPE 8, then 4×6 at 85 % of the top set, 180 s rest. Chest-supported dumbbell row 4×8–12 at RPE 8, 120 s. Lateral raise 3×12–15 at RPE 8 and rear delt fly 3×12–15 at RPE 8 as a superset, 60 s. The swing session: 12 minutes on the minute, 12 swings each minute at RPE 7, starting at 40 lb (18.14 kg in Hevy); it grows two minutes at a time to a cap of 16 minutes, and reps can rise to 15.
- **Tuesday – PT session at the gym**, alternating chest and back (about 6 chest, 6 lat and 3 biceps sets) with legs and core (about 6 quad, 4 glute and 4 ab sets). Joe doesn't control its content.
- **Wednesday – pull-up volume and core (75 min).** Scapular pull-ups 2×6–8 at RPE 5 as activation; negative pull-ups 3×2–4 at RPE 8 (lower for 4–5 s, lengthening to 6 s then 8 s, then the vest once every set hits 4); banded pull-ups 4×5–8 at RPE 8, moving to a lighter band when every set hits 8; flexed-arm hang 2×20 s; lying leg raise 3×10–15 at RPE 8 and suitcase carry 4×30 s as a superset; single-leg standing calf raise 3×10–15 at RPE 8.
- **Friday – strict pull-up test, squat and legs (75 min).** One strict pull-up attempt at RPE 10; back squat warm-ups of 5, 3 and 2, a top set of 5 at RPE 8, then 4×5 at 85 %; Romanian deadlift 3×6–10 at RPE 8; dumbbell split squat 3×8–12 at RPE 8; dumbbell shoulder press 3×8–12 at RPE 8; single-leg calf raise 3×10–15 at RPE 8; ab wheel 3×6–12 at RPE 8.
- **Saturday – bench, back and arms (90 min).** Bench warm-ups of 8, 5 and 3, a top set of 5 at RPE 8, then 4×6; barbell bent-over row 4×6–10 at RPE 8; incline dumbbell bench 3×8–12 at RPE 8; dip negatives 3×3–5 at RPE 8; overhead triceps extension 3×10–15 at RPE 8; lateral raise 3×12–15 at RPE 8.
- **Sunday – deadlift and legs (90 min).** Deadlift warm-ups of 5 and 3, a top set of 5 at RPE 8, then 3×5; Bulgarian split squat 3×8–12 at RPE 8; barbell hip thrust 3×8–12 at RPE 8; banded pull-up 3×5–8 at RPE 8; dumbbell bicep curl 3×8–12 at RPE 8; hammer curl 3×10–12 at RPE 8; farmers walk 3×30 s starting at 50 lb per hand (45.36 kg in Hevy).
- **Optional:** a strength circuit (goblet squat 4×10, ring push-up 4×12, kettlebell swing 4×12 at 40 lb, mountain climber 4×16; 4 rounds, up to 6, 16-minute cap, RPE 8) and a daily dead hang of 2×20 s at RPE 5.

Weekly dose targets: 10 hard sets per muscle; 5 for bench, 5 for overhead press, 5 for squat, 4 for deadlift; 10 pull-up sets a week, counting negatives and banded reps. A deload triggers after 6 hard weeks: sets cut 40 %, loads unchanged, RPE capped at 8, and the priority lifts get tested.

## The proposed change

Add **Incline Curl (Dumbbell), 3 sets of 8–12 at RPE 8, 75 s rest, double progression** (add weight once every set reaches 12) as the last exercise on Monday, after the lateral raise / rear delt fly superset. Cues: bench at about 45°, arms hanging straight down behind the torso, elbows stay back for a full stretch at the bottom, no shoulder swing.

The reason that would be recorded with the new version: direct biceps work was six sets in one session (Sunday's curls and hammer curls); an incline curl on Monday makes it nine over two days, trains the biceps at long muscle length, and keeps the lightest lifting day inside its cap. Joe did incline curls under his previous program, so the movement isn't new to him. It is dumbbell work, which matches his stated preference for direct biceps training. On top of that, the PT's chest-and-back Tuesday brings roughly 3 more biceps sets every other week.

**No starting load is set for the curl.** When next week's plan is drafted, the engine will derive it from his logged history if it finds incline curls there; otherwise Joe will need to name a starting dumbbell.

## What the dry run says

The check ran without any violation, so adoption would go through. It would record:

- a **fourth program version**, an amendment (not a redesign), starting at rotation week A;
- the block that opened on 1 Nov 2026 **continues unbroken** — no reset of the deload count or the progress baseline;
- the only difference from the version in force is **one line added to Monday**; no sessions added or removed, no defaults filled in by the engine;
- Monday's time estimate becomes **53 minutes against its 75-minute cap**. The others: Wednesday 39 of 75, Friday 65 of 75, Saturday 65 of 90, Sunday 65 of 90.

Before checking, the engine pulled from Hevy (the window ran from 20:40 to 20:53 UTC on 4 Nov 2026) and found nothing new: no workouts, weigh-ins, routine or folder changes.

Adopting writes only to the coaching record. **Nothing changes in Hevy until the next weekly plan is drafted and pushed**, which is a separate approval step. Running the same file a second time does nothing; undoing it later would need another amendment.

## Warnings, and what they mean

**1. Three Hevy routines have drifted from the week plan approved on 2 Nov 2026.** Joe (or something) has edited them in Hevy since they were pushed. The engine lists what differs by position but names the routines only by reference, so I can describe the shape and give my best read:

- One routine: the duration of the first exercise's second set changed. That pattern fits the daily dead hang (one exercise, 2×20 s).
- One routine: the reps of the first exercise's sets 5, 6 and 7 changed, and the weight on the second exercise's sets 1–3. That fits a barbell top-set day where he rewrote the back-off reps and the second lift's loads.
- One routine: the weight on the third exercise's sets 1–4, the duration of the fourth exercise's sets 1–2, and the weight on the sixth exercise's sets 1–3. That fits the Wednesday pull-up session (banded pull-up resistance, flexed-arm hang time, carry load).

For training, this is informational: it does not block the change and it doesn't alter the plan. The practical consequence is that **the next push to Hevy will overwrite his edits** unless they are recorded as overrides on the next week plan. If his edits were deliberate (for instance he found the prescribed loads wrong), the coach should find out what he changed and why before next week's plan goes out. Either an override on the next plan or the next push clears it.

**2. The deadlift target of 4 hard sets a week sits below the 5–15 band the maintenance phase expects.** This one was already acknowledged when the third version was adopted, with the reasoning that Sunday's deadlift is written as a top set plus three back-offs (four hard sets), Friday's Romanian deadlift carries the hinge pattern, and the PT sometimes adds deadlifts on Tuesdays — so a target of 5 would flag under-target every single week the session is done as written. The acknowledgement carries over to the new version. Nothing to do unless the coach wants to change the deadlift session itself.

**3. The Friday strict pull-up test line doesn't match the hypertrophy emphasis.** A single all-out rep at RPE 10 held at fixed terms is a test, not a growth set, so the engine flags it as off-emphasis. That is intended — it's how Joe tracks progress toward five strict pull-ups, and his coaching notes say strict sets become real work only once the test passes about five. The output was cut off partway through this warning, so I cannot confirm whether it already carries an acknowledgement from the third version or whether anything followed it. I'd want one more look at the full warning list before adoption to be sure nothing further is waiting there.

## What Joe needs to agree to

- Monday gains a fifth exercise: three sets of incline dumbbell curls, 8–12 reps at RPE 8, after the shoulder superset, with about 53 minutes of work estimated inside the 75-minute cap (and the swing session still sits alongside it).
- Direct biceps work rises from 6 sets on Sunday to 9 sets across Sunday and Monday, before counting what the PT does.
- He names a starting dumbbell for the curl if his history doesn't supply one.
- He confirms his recent hand edits in Hevy — what he changed and whether to keep them — so the next weekly push either preserves them as overrides or correctly overwrites them.
- He understands this is recorded as a fourth version of the program with the biceps reasoning above as its stated cause, the current block keeps running without reset, and his Hevy routines change only at the next weekly plan push.

Here's what the change looks like, ready for your yes.

**Monday becomes**

1. Overhead press: warm-ups of 5 and 3, top set of 5 at RPE 8, then 4×6 at 85 %, 180 s rest
2. Chest-supported dumbbell row 4×8–12 at RPE 8, 120 s
3. Lateral raise 3×12–15 at RPE 8 and rear delt fly 3×12–15 at RPE 8, superset, 60 s
4. **Incline curl (dumbbell) 3×8–12 at RPE 8, 75 s rest** — new, last in the session

Bench at about 45°, arms hanging straight down behind you, elbows kept back so you get the full stretch at the bottom, no shoulder swing. Add weight once every set reaches 12. Monday's estimate goes to 53 minutes against the 75 you have, and the kettlebell swing session alongside it is unchanged.

Nothing else moves. Direct biceps work goes from 6 sets on Sunday to 9 across Sunday and Monday, before the extra 3 or so your PT adds every other Tuesday. This is a small amendment to the program you're already on: the block that started on 1 November keeps running, so your deload count and progress tracking carry on uninterrupted. Your Hevy routines won't change until next week's plan is drafted and pushed, which you'll approve separately.

Two things to settle:

**Starting weight.** If your old logs have incline curls, next week's plan will pick the load from there. If they don't, name a dumbbell you'd start with — aim for one where 8 reps is hard but clean.

**Your Hevy edits.** Three of your routines have been changed by hand since the week plan went out: it looks like the dead hang time, the back-off reps and second-lift loads on one of the barbell days, and the band, hang time and carry load on the Wednesday pull-up session. If those were deliberate, tell me what you changed and why and I'll carry them into next week's plan. If I don't, the next push will put the original numbers back.

I'll give the full set of notes one last read before recording, but the biceps change itself is clear to go. Shall I record it?
